hypothesis: Method sensitivity check, not a candidate. (a) Positive control: a hand-written repository-aware patch-writing skill (conda env activation, each repo's real test command, reproduce-fix-test workflow; written before any assessment data, from general knowledge) raises Haiku 5.5's agentic SWE-bench Lite resolve rate by at least 0.10 versus the untouched base skill and the fixed policy. (b) Negative control: a sabotage skill (edit comments only, never code) in the deterministic_random slot scores below the untouched base. Label design=positive_control; never counts toward auto-apply.
benchmark: SWE-bench Lite, agentic (Hermes terminal+file tools in the task image, no network), SWE-bench/SWE-bench_Lite harness
random_skill: NEGATIVE CONTROL: ~/.caduceus/swe/neg (sabotage: edit comments only, never code)
decision_rule: Units: 60 sealed assessment tasks, one agent run per arm; resolved (1) or not (0) by the SWE-bench harness; empty diff or non-applying patch scores 0; infra errors exclude. Positive control passes iff candidate minus untouched_base, minus fixed_policy, and minus negative control all have bootstrap lower bound > 0 and mean >= 0.10. Sensitivity check passes iff untouched_base minus negative control has lower bound > 0. Interpretation: sensitivity fails => pipeline broken; sensitivity passes and positive control fails => skill text cannot move this executor here by 0.10; both pass => method can detect real skill effects and earlier nulls are informative.
